target: रोहन इस बार ज़रूर पास होगा।
english: Rohan will definitely pass this time.
reason: Gender mismatch: रूबी is a woman's name but the verb is masculine होगा, so the model sentence is grammatically wrong. Swapped in a male name to keep the same ज़रूर + future pattern.

target: डॉक्टर ने मुझे नई दवा दी है।
english: The doctor has given me a new medicine.
reason: Officialese/literary register: औषधि and परीक्षण करना belong to formal written Hindi, not the everyday speech being taught (दवा is the spoken word).

target: कचरा हर सुबह गाड़ी में उठाया जाता है।
english: The garbage is picked up by the truck every morning.
reason: Reads like a recycling PSA with no subject; vacuous as a spoken line. Replacement keeps the impersonal passive but describes something a learner actually says about their street.

target: तेज़ बारिश ने हमारी फ़सल को नुक़सान पहुँचाया।
english: The heavy rain damaged our crops.
reason: Niche vocabulary: जंगली सूअर (wild boar) is content a learner will essentially never use. Same ने + नुक़सान पहुँचाना structure with an everyday cause.

target: वह कंधे पर बैग रखकर स्कूल चला गया।
english: He put the bag on his shoulder and left for school.
reason: Novelistic narration (सोच में डूबा था) plus the rare word ठोढ़ी; nobody speaks like this. Replacement keeps the body-part + कर-participle pattern in ordinary speech.

target: जितनी जल्दी निकलोगे, उतनी जल्दी पहुँच जाओगे।
english: The earlier you leave, the earlier you'll get there.
reason: Proverb/moralising motto ('the more you work, the more reward you get'). Replacement teaches the same जितना...उतना correlative with a practical everyday statement.

target: रोज़ सुबह टहलना मेरी आदत है।
english: Walking every morning is my habit.
reason: Preachy civic slogan about tax being everyone's duty. Replacement keeps the infinitive-as-subject + possessive + है pattern with a natural personal statement.

target: विजय आज नहीं आएगा, यानी काम कल ही होगा।
english: Vijay won't come today, which means the work will only happen tomorrow.
reason: Padded tautology: the second clause just restates the first ('his effort succeeded, that is his hard work paid off'). Replacement uses यानी for a real inference.

target: दुकान बंद है, यानी हमें कल आना पड़ेगा।
english: The shop is closed, which means we'll have to come tomorrow.
reason: Same circular padding as hi-2443, with the two clauses swapped. Replacement keeps यानी but draws an actual consequence.

target: रश्मि ने अपने फ़ैसले के बारे में माँ को बताया।
english: Rashmi told her mother about her decision.
reason: फ़ैसले पर अमल करना is news/bureaucratic register, not everyday speech. Replacement keeps ने + past transitive with the same फ़ैसला vocabulary.

target: प्रतियोगिता में उसे पहला इनाम मिला।
english: He got first prize in the competition.
reason: Niche content plus stilted wording: spoken Hindi says गोल्ड मेडल, not सोने का तमग़ा. Replacement keeps the मिलना (experiencer) pattern with common words.

target: मंदिर में सबको प्रसाद बाँटा गया।
english: Prasad was distributed to everyone at the temple.
reason: Mixes भंडारा (Hindu community meal) with लंगर (Sikh community meal) in one sentence, which no native speaker would do, and the English gloss is redundant. Replacement keeps the passive + community-event context.
